title: Model decomposition for serving-aware evaluations
author: Aisha Patel
body:
SUMMARY:
This playbook describes a recommended, repeatable process to decompose large monolithic models into serving-aware subcomponents for evaluation. The goal is to make evals, quantization checks, and regression triage reflect the real production serving stack (tokenization, adapter layers, kv-cache behavior, quant kernels, and network shims) so that performance, quality, and rollback decisions are grounded in operational reality rather than idealized model binaries.

CONTENTS:
- Motivation and scope
- Decomposition strategy and component contracts
- Evaluation harness integration patterns
- Quantization compatibility matrix and validations
- Onboarding checklist and promotion gates
- Regression triage adjustments and runbook
- Example manifests and CLI examples

1) MOTIVATION AND SCOPE
Decomposing models into serving-aware components reduces blind spots that cause regressions during rollouts. Typical blind spots include: quantized kernel mismatches, tokenizer differences, KV cache truncation, and custom adapter layers that change attention shape. This doc applies to:
- Large decoder-only or encoder-decoder models being promoted to Redwood hosted/dedicated/private runtime.
- Model variants (FP16, 4-bit/Quantized, adapter-fused versions).
- Evals that must simulate realistic per-request state (KV-cache warm/cold, streaming chunk sizes, prefix-caching).

2) DECOMPOSITION STRATEGY
High-level decomposition targets the following components:
- Tokenizer layer (tokenize/normalize/encoder mapping)
- Front-end adapters (prompt prep, input filters, instruction wrappers)
- Core model weight blob (architecture + weights)
- KV-cache/serving-state shim (serialization format + truncation policy)
- Quantization/exec profile (kernel selection, op-fusion knobs)
- Network shim (protocol differences: gRPC vs HTTP/streaming)
- Post-processing (detokenization, response filters, function-call wiring)

For each component define a contract: input shape, version, deterministic behavior, and a lightweight compatibility test. Example contract entry (single line):
- tokenizer:v2 -> deterministic mapping for control chars U+000A..U+001F, supports legacy byte-fallback mode.

3) EVALUATION HARNESS INTEGRATION PATTERNS
Goal: Make the harness exercise component interactions instead of only invoking a single model artifact. Patterns below can be implemented in the eval harness (serving-side adapters or evaluator SDK).

Pattern A — Component-anchored scenario (recommended)
- Create test scenarios that explicitly exercise boundaries (e.g., tokenizer + quant kernel).
- Harness config contains component overrides: tokenizer_image, kernel_profile, kv_policy.
- Run each scenario in two modes: ideal (reference binary) and serving-simulated (component chain).

Pattern B — Proxy-in-the-loop shadow run
- Deploy a light-weight proxy that emulates runtime shims (kv-cache, rate-limiter) and send real traffic or synthetic probes through it to the model binary.

Pattern C — Binary-only baseline (keep for continuity)
- Maintain the legacy binary-only tests to track delta vs decomposed runs.

4) QUANTIZATION COMPATIBILITY MATRIX & VALIDATIONS
Maintain a per-model matrix describing which quant profiles are compatible with which kernel families and runtime flags. Required columns (table below):

| column | description | example |
|---|---|---|
| model_family | short id | redwood-7b-v2 |
| base_precision | stored precision of canonical artifact | fp16 |
| quant_profile | label for quant config | q4_0_fast, q2_k_vmap |
| kernel_family | kernel selection (cuda/rocm/auto) | cuda-sm80-opt |
| known_issues | short notes, link to bug | bias-drift-on-long-context |
| validation_status | pass/partial/fail | partial |
Validation steps (automated):
- Unit tests: numeric rounding checks on a canonical token slice (max 512 tokens). Thresholds: cosine similarity > 0.996 on embeddings; response-levenshtein <= 8 on expected outputs for templated prompts.
- Streaming/kv tests: verify deterministic continuation across 3 chunk-boundaries.
- Perf tests: 95th percentile per-token latency within 1.4x of baseline for the target hardware.
- Stability tests: run 1000 randomized prompts, compute Response Stability Index (RSI) and raise alert if RSI change > 0.05 vs baseline.

5) ONBOARDING CHECKLIST (DECOMPOSED PROMOTION)
Follow these steps to promote a decomposed model to staging/production:

1. Create a decomposition manifest (see example below) and store in model registry.
2. Run component compatibility validator (tokenizer, quant_profile, kernel selection).
3. Execute a smoke eval (10 canonical prompts) in both ideal and serving-simulated modes; attach diffs.
4. Run a 1-hour shadow replay with probe-sampling rate 0.5% for production-simulated telemetry.
5. Evaluate quality gates: embedding cosine, RSI delta, and hallucination sentinel rate — all must be within configured budgets.
6. Run throughput/failure injection tests with scaled concurrency to target QPS and CPU/GPU utilization thresholds.
7. If any gate fails, open a regression ticket and follow the regression triage runbook section below.
8. On success, create a canary rollout plan with automatic rollback triggers.

Required artifacts checklist (table):
- Decomposition manifest (YAML)
- Component hashes and provenance links
- Eval diffs and artifacts (raw outputs, metrics, logs)
- Perf telemetry and kernel selection logs

Example decomposition manifest (YAML snippet):
---
model_id: redwood-7b-v2-decomposed
components:
  tokenizer: redwood-tokenizer:v2
  adapter: instruction-fuse-v1
  core_weights: redwood-7b-v2-fp16
  quant_profile: q4_0_fast
  kernel_family: cuda-sm80-opt
kv_policy: "fixed-window-8192"
postproc: "functioncall-safe-v1"
---

6) REGRESSION TRIAGE RUNBOOK ADJUSTMENTS
When a regression is detected between ideal and serving-simulated evals or by production monitoring, apply this triage sequence tailored to decomposed artifacts: 

1. Reproduce: rerun the failing probe in both modes with logs and deterministic seeds.
2. Isolate component: swap to the reference component for the suspected boundary (e.g., replace quant kernels with reference fp16 exec) and measure delta.
3. Binary search within components: if replacing tokenizer fixes the issue, examine tokenizer diffs and unicode normalization changes.
4. Check kernel and operator-level numerics (compare op-level outputs for the problematic token range).
5. If quantization suspected, run the quant-profile numeric check and a mixed-precision fallback test.
6. If KV-cache suspected, replay conversation fragments with varying truncation and verify decoder continuation.
7. Create a regression ticket with these fields: failing_probe_id, component_diff_snapshot, numeric-diff-sample, perf-delta, suggested-mitigation.
8. If rollback is required, use the promoted artifact with identical component contracts to avoid recurrence.

7) METRICS AND SLOS (EXAMPLE)
- Quality SLO (canary threshold): 95% of canonical prompts must have response similarity >= 0.98 vs reference.
- RSI budget: RSI delta <= 0.04 on promoted slice pools.
- Latency SLO: p95 per-token latency <= 1.4x baseline for dedicated hardware targets.
- Regression severity matrix:
  - Sev1: >10% of production probes failing function-call safeties or hallucination sentinels.
  - Sev2: measurable quality drift across top-10 slices (>5% drop).

8) EXAMPLE CLI WORKFLOW
- Validate manifest: redwood-eval-tool validate --manifest decomposed-manifest.yaml
- Run decomposed smoke: redwood-eval-tool run --manifest decomposed-manifest.yaml --mode serving-simulated --scenarios smoke
- Compare diffs: redwood-eval-tool diff --left ideal --right simulated --out diffs.json
- Upload artifacts: redwood-registry upload-artifacts --model redwood-7b-v2-decomposed --path ./artifacts/

9) OPERATIONAL NOTES AND OWNERSHIP
- Ownership: model-onboarding team owns the manifest and validation pipeline; applied-ml owns probe design and quality metrics; eng-serving-runtime owns kernel families and runtime flags.
- Audit: all decomposed promotions must include a signed promotion note in the registry and the eval artifacts attached.
- Observability: ensure per-component feature flags are instrumented and surfaced on the Redwood Console (tokenizer mismatch rate, quant-fallback counts, kv-truncation events).

10) APPENDIX: TROUBLESHOOTING QUICK HITS
- Tokenization mismatch: compare token ids for first 256 characters; if mismatch, check normalization table and byte-fallback mode.
- Stochastic divergence after quant: run 100 deterministic seeds and measure stderr of token logits at each layer.
- Streaming boundary artifacts: simulate chunk sizes of 1, 64, 256 tokens and compare decoder continuations.
